summary: Recap of last week's benchmarks: intermittent queue jitter observed at burst windows when concurrency moves above ~48. Team walked through continuous batching, KV cache warmup, and proposed an adaptive concurrency cap + slightly larger batch window to reduce jitter while preserving p99 latency. Agreed on a 24-hour steady-state run and several deliverables (scripts, configs, security docs).
topics: security and audit concerns for POC
transcript:
[00:00] Ari: okay everyone, uh thanks for joining, we're 10am PT. quick check — did you all get the throughput sheet i dropped?
[00:12] Liam: yeah, Liam here, i pulled it, saw the two runs, the one at 32 concurrent is neat but then the 64 run had weird p95 spikes around the .9 second mark, is that what you saw?
[00:25] Sofia: yeah so the 64 run shows queuing jitter, looks like batches are sometimes small then suddenly big, we think it ties to the batch window plus backlog shape, also maybe the KV cache warmup wasn't consistent.
[00:38] Priya: so is that network noise or runtime? we saw CPU on the host jitter too during the runs, curious if it's GC or the compilation path.
[00:49] Ari: good q; my read — and this is preliminary — is it's mostly batching and concurrency interplay. when concurrency crosses about 48 the continuous batching heuristics start forming mixed batches. some requests wait longer for batch fill, then next window gets overloaded.
[01:05] Marcus: so the p99 goes from 220ms to near 1.1s during those spikes, unacceptable for our user SLAs. we'd rather cap concurrency and accept higher steady token cost than have big spikes.
[01:18] Sofia: that's reasonable. we can try an adaptive cap approach: keep concurrency target at 48 for the hot path, and allow short bursts to 64 with a quick fallback to a lighter model or to the hosted pool. fallback would protect tail latency.
[01:33] Liam: fallback sounds nice but what about cost — if it routes to hosted pool, we'll pay more. need to quantify.
[01:39] Ari: yep, we should run two configs in parallel: 48 fixed cap, and the adaptive 48->64 with a fallback to a cheaper quantized variant beyond 64. i'll share estimated cost delta in the sheet.
[01:51] Priya: also want to call out KV caching — in the last run the cache miss rate was like 18% at steady which spikes to 35% during bursts. that makes batch sizes vary because prefix reuse isn't consistent.
[02:05] Sofia: for that we suggested a short prefetch step for known prefixes — just priming the KV for the session. ill send sample scripts. it's not perfect but narrows the miss tail.
[02:16] Liam: can you explain the prefetch briefly? is it blocking request?
[02:20] Sofia: it's async priming right after session start, so it warms the KV in parallel. you can tune the TTL and keep a light in-memory index to avoid heavy remote calls.
[02:30] Marcus: okay, but does that change cold-starts for new users? we have many short-lived sessions.
[02:34] Ari: good point. for short sessions, prefetch gives diminishing returns. the pattern we saw indicates most of your traffic is medium sessions, so prefetch helps; for micro sessions we should rely more on batching heuristics and lower concurrency.
[02:48] Liam: what's the plan for the 24-hour run? replicating production traffic shape?
[02:53] Sofia: yes, we want the Bridgepoint production mix — you gave us the sample histogram last month. we'll run two variants back-to-back: adaptive vs fixed cap, each 24h, and collect p50/p95/p99, batch distributions, KV miss, and host resource metrics.
[03:08] Priya: we'll need the exact SDK commands to run — last time we scripted it but we had different headers so telemetry mapping was off.
[03:16] Sofia: i'll send a canonical curl+python example with telemetry tags and a standard prometheus exporters layout.
[03:22] Ari: also we should instrument queue depth histogram and a batch-size histogram in the payload so we can join them in the sheet.
[03:29] Liam: agreed. also on the routing fallback — what's the expected behavior if fallback triggers? does it change model outputs?
[03:36] Ari: yes minor difference — fallback uses a 3-bit quantized variant optimized for latency. we validated quality on your eval set, it's within your threshold but we flagged a couple prompts where it paraphrases slightly. we'll list those.
[03:49] Marcus: need to surface that to product stakeholders; we prefer deterministic output for billing-critical flows.
[03:54] Priya: security check: we need confirmation on KMS integration and where logs live. do we get redwood audit logs per request?
[04:01] Ari: yes, we can provide per-request audit logs in the console for Dedicated and we redact PII; for Private deploy you can plug KMS/HSM. i'll attach SOC2 and the KMS integration note.
[04:11] Priya: good. also SSO — we want SAML mapped to role-based controls before we expand.
[04:16] Sofia: SAML and RBAC are supported; we'll share the SSO checklist.
[04:20] Liam: timeline: procurement is roughly 6 weeks, but if POC shows steady tails under 350ms p99 we can accelerate.
[04:28] Marcus: what's our success criteria again for the POC?
[04:31] Ari: agreed success: sustained p99 < 350ms during production-shaped load, cost delta under 15% vs current infra, and SOC2 + KMS review passed.
[04:42] Liam: realistic? maybe 12% cost is okay.
[04:45] Ari: okay we'll target 12%.
[04:47] Sofia: technical note — when tuning batch window, smaller window helps p50 but hurts throughput, larger window improves throughput but can increase p99 if it batches cold requests; the sweet spot often sits where average batch size is 6-8 for your token distribution.
[05:02] Priya: can we get recommended settings?
[05:04] Sofia: yes, current recommendation: base window 20ms, max wait 60ms, adaptive cap 48 with burst to 64 for 200ms windows only, and KV prefetch on session start for known prefixes. i'll put exact config in the doc.
[05:21] Liam: last run we saw 18% miss rate, can you put expected drop with prefetch?
[05:25] Sofia: expect miss rate drop to ~6-8% if prefetch warms the top-100 prefixes.
[05:31] Marcus: any risk of overloading Redis or KV store with prefetch?
[05:34] Sofia: you can throttle prefetch calls and stagger them; the script uses exponential backoff and a small jitter to avoid thundering herd.
[05:43] Ari: action item summary — i'll share configs and an updated sheet; Bridgepoint runs the 24h tests; Sofia provides scripts; Marcus and Priya confirm legal and security asks.
[05:53] Liam: great, let's reconvene next Wednesday same time unless we see issues. thanks all.
[05:58] [End of recording]
